reason: H0 exercises meshopt_SimplifyPermissive only through meshopt_simplify. Both attribute-aware entry points pass options=0, so the harness cannot cover permissive attribute-seam/complex/fringe collapses through meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes or meshopt_simplifyWithUpdate. This is material because the S1 logic in performEdgeCollapses specifically changes remapping for Kind_Complex and Kind_Fringe wedges using getComplexTarget, while classifyVertices creates those kinds under meshopt_SimplifyPermissive. H0 also derives all vertex data from srand(buffer[0]), limiting geometry to 256 generated buffers instead of allowing the fuzzer to construct targeted coincident-position wedges and divergent attributes.
evidence: meshopt_simplify is called with meshopt_SimplifyPermissive, but meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes and meshopt_simplifyWithUpdate are each called with options argument 0.

performEdgeCollapses changes the Kind_Complex/Kind_Fringe branch from applying getComplexTarget to every wedge to assigning collapse_remap[i0] = i1 and applying getComplexTarget only to subsequent wedges.
classifyVertices assigns Kind_Fringe or Kind_Complex only inside the `options & meshopt_SimplifyPermissive` branch.
H0 consumes only buffer[0] for srand and generates vb with rand() % 10; remaining fuzz bytes control ib, so arbitrary vertex positions and attributes cannot be encoded.
recommended_action: Add permissive-mode calls for meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes and meshopt_simplifyWithUpdate, and decode fuzzer bytes into positions, attributes, and topology. Seed or structure inputs to create coincident-position wedge cycles with differing attributes and border/non-border cases so both Kind_Complex and Kind_Fringe remapping paths are exercised.
